title: Stabilize softmax inputs before temperature scaling
body:
## Summary

Use at least float32 arithmetic and, when shifting is requested, subtract the maximum before dividing by temperature. The existing temperature floor and `shift=False` option remain in place.

## Impact

A large shared offset can overflow during temperature division before the existing stabilizing shift is reached, producing `inf - inf` and NaN probabilities. Half-precision label-quality scores can also overflow at low temperatures despite all their input values being in [0, 1]. This affects softmin aggregation and the public token-classification label-quality API.

Moving the shift ahead of scaling preserves softmax's translation invariance and avoids overflow caused by a common offset. Promoting half-precision arithmetic prevents the demonstrated low-temperature failures; integer inputs are also converted before subtraction so their differences do not wrap.

## Testing

- Added 22 regression cases: upstream has 10 failures and 12 passes; all 22 pass with this change.
- New tests plus complete existing numerics and token-classification modules: 73 passed, with four existing warnings.
- Covered float16/32/64 values, four axis choices, large common offsets, signed/unsigned inputs, two actual softmin aggregators and the public token-classification scoring API. References use SciPy in a safe float64 range or explicitly known normalized probabilities. Inputs are checked for mutation.
- Project-pinned Black 25.12.0 and `git diff --check` passed.

## Links/References

Checked #667, #826 and #1114 and the complete numerical helper history. The previous stability changes still divide before shifting; all-state low-temperature/shift/float16 searches found no equivalent change.

## Reviewer Notes

This covers the demonstrated low-temperature and common-offset cases. It does not claim every extreme floating-point input can be processed without any overflow warning.
